answer: A policy loan lets you borrow against part of a variable life insurance policy’s cash value. Borrowing reduces that cash value, which can make the policy more likely to lapse, and may also reduce the death benefit. You will typically owe interest on the amount borrowed. Policy loans are typically not subject to surrender charges, but that does not mean they are cost-free. Review your policy’s loan terms and consider how an outstanding loan could affect the policy.
